description: Benchmark fixtures for the M2 model evaluation (SDD §8).
notes: Each case is a message a real B1 Indonesian learner might plausibly send,
written in the code-switched register the app is built for. `expect` lists
the rule ids a competent tutor should catch.
Three properties are deliberately built in:
1. CLEAN CASES. Six messages contain no English error at all. A model that
invents corrections for these is worse than useless — it teaches wrong
rules and demoralises the learner (SDD §10). False positives are scored
separately from misses for exactly this reason.
2. INDONESIAN THAT MUST NOT BE TOUCHED. Every case mixes languages. Any
correction whose `original` is Indonesian is a policy violation, not a
grammar mistake, and is counted as such.
3. MULTI-ERROR CASES. Some messages carry more errors than the three-per-
turn cap allows. These test prioritisation, not recall: `expect` lists
everything present, and scoring only requires the model to find some of
